a result through contract labour or supplies

options_hindi: I, II और III
II, III और IV
I, II और IV
I, III और IV
questions.question_english:
Consider the following conditions relating to
“Contract Labour”:
I.
Hired in connection with the work of an
establishment.
II. Hired through a contractor.
III. Hired with the mandatory written consent of
the principal employer.
IV. Hired for hire or reward.
Which of the above are the essential statutory
components of the definition under Section 2(1)
(b) of the Contract Labour (Regulation and
Abolition) Act, 1970?
options_english: I, II and III
II, III and IV
I, II and IV
I, III and IV
questions.explanation_english:
I, II and IV
Section 2(1)(b) specifies three fundamental
components: being hired in connection with
the work of an establishment, being hired by
or through a contractor, and working for hire
or reward. Written consent of the principal
employer is not a legal requirement, as hiring can
occur with or without the employer’s knowledge.
questions.explanation_hindi: कानूनी परिभाषा में प्रतिष्ठान के काम से जुड़ा नियोजन, ठेकेदार के माध्यम से नियुक्ति और पारिश्रमिक के बदले काम शामिल है; प्रमुख नियोक्ता की लिखित सहमति अलग अनिवार्य तत्व नहीं है।
key_facts: Correct option (English): I, II and IV

Assertion (A): The Principal Employer is
ultimately liable to provide welfare amenities if
the contractor fails to do so within the prescribed
time.
Reason (R): Section 20 of the Act imposes a
primary responsibility on the contractor and
a vicarious/residual liability on the Principal
Employer to ensure worker welfare.
options_english:
Both A and R are true and R is the correct

Both A and R are true but R is not the

Assertion A correctly identifies the Principal
Employer’s legal duty to provide welfare
amenities if the contractor defaults. Reason R
accurately explains this, as Section 20 creates
primary liability for the contractor and vicarious
liability for the Principal Employer to protect
worker welfare.

questions.question_english:

the
following
statements
about

Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition)
Act, 1970:
I.
The Central or State Advisory Board may
constitute such committees as it thinks fit.
II. These committees must exclusively consist
of members of the Board.
III. The committee may co-opt persons who are
not members of the Board to assist them.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
options_english: I and II only

existing Board members.

unregistered establishment can legally employ
contract labour.
Reason (R): Section 9 of the Contract Labour
(Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970 expressly
prohibits the employment of contract labour in

questions.question_english:
Consider the following actions taken by a
Principal regarding outsourced staff:
I.
Checking the contractor’s valid labour
licence.
II. Depositing EPF directly into the workers’
accounts by bypassing the agency.
III. Ensuring a first-aid box is available on the
school premises.
IV. Authorizing a teacher to witness the payment
of wages.
Which of the above actions are correct and in
accordance with the law?
options_english: I, II and III
I, III and IV
II, III and IV
I, II, III and IV
questions.explanation_english:
I, III and IV
Statements I, III, and IV are correct actions:
verifying contractor licences, keeping first-
aid boxes available on site, and delegating a
representative to witness wage disbursements.
Statement II is incorrect as EPF deposits are
managed through statutory portal returns rather
than direct worker payments.
questions.explanation_hindi: वैध लाइसेंस जाँचना, प्राथमिक उपचार की सुविधा सुनिश्चित करना और मजदूरी भुगतान के समय अधिकृत प्रतिनिधि रखना उचित कदम हैं। एजेंसी को दरकिनार कर EPF जमा करना सामान्य निर्धारित प्रक्रिया नहीं है।
